kept.excerpt: The Islamic Republic of Iran and the United States of America commit to negotiating and achieving the final Deal, in maximum 60 days extendable with mutual consent.
kept.publisher: The American Presidency Project — archived MOU text
kept.relevance: Establishes the negotiation framework and its provision for extension, which helps distinguish an unfinished agreement from definitive termination of US participation.

kept.excerpt: President Donald J. Trump and Vice President JD Vance have secured a historic breakthrough by signing a Memorandum of Understanding with Iran. The White House release describes the agreement as reopening the Strait of Hormuz to free navigation.
kept.relevance: Provides a dated official US acknowledgment of the MOU and the administration's initial commitment to its implementation.

kept.excerpt: President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that the memorandum of understanding signed with Iran to end the conflict was "over."
kept.relevance: Records a presidential declaration requiring scrutiny under the resolution rule's distinction between ending the ceasefire or MOU and definitively ending participation in negotiations.

kept.excerpt: “The United States is still committed to finding a resolution, and technical talks continue,” reads a statement attributed to a senior US official that the White House has sent to querying reporters. “The MOU is performance-based, and Iran’s actions constitute failed performance at an unacceptable level,” the official adds.
kept.relevance: Reports a White House-distributed statement explicitly affirming continued technical talks after Trump's declaration that the framework was over.

kept.excerpt: “The Islamic Republic of Iran has asked us to continue ‘talks.’ We have agreed to do so, but the United States has stated to them, in no uncertain terms, that the ceasefire is OVER!” Trump wrote, on his Truth Social platform.
kept.relevance: Quotes the president explicitly agreeing to continue talks while declaring the ceasefire over, directly addressing the distinction central to the resolution criteria.

kept.excerpt: Iran said Monday it will not fulfill its obligations under the Pakistan-mediated memorandum of understanding with the US as long as Washington continues to violate its commitments. Commenting on recent diplomatic contacts, Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said diplomacy remained “an available tool” despite the military escalation. He said Iran had held meetings with Qatari and Omani officials in recent days and remained in contact with Pakistan.
kept.relevance: Documents conditional Iranian nonperformance alongside continuing diplomatic contacts, supplying context without treating Iranian actions as a US termination announcement.

kept.excerpt: The conflict between Iran and the United States has intensified in recent days and an interim deal to end the fighting has collapsed less than a month after it was signed. The Memorandum of Understanding was supposed to halt all military operations and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial waterway for global oil and gas. It also set the stage for further negotiations intended to lead to a permanent peace deal and an agreement on Iran's nuclear program within 60 days.
kept.relevance: Provides a near-cutoff assessment of deteriorating implementation, while its description of the interim deal's collapse does not itself establish an official US termination of negotiations.

kept.excerpt: Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said on Saturday that Tehran has suspended its commitments to a recent memorandum of understanding after “the US violated its commitments.” “We have also suspended our commitments, we are not implementing them, and we are busy defending the country,” he added. The military escalation comes despite a Pakistan-brokered memorandum of understanding signed in June to end the war and reach a lasting peace agreement.
kept.relevance: Supplies cutoff-date evidence of Iranian suspension and worsening relations, with attribution that prevents an Iranian characterization from being mistaken for an authorized US withdrawal announcement.

search_notes: Frozen evidence cutoff: 2026-07-18. This is an evidence pack, not a resolution determination or a claim of exhaustive coverage. The supplied resolution text ends mid-sentence, so no missing rule language was inferred.
